name: Lakefront and Ohinemutu
tagline: The old Maori village on the lake, where the steam comes up between the houses
description: Ohinemutu is a living village on the lakeshore where Te Arawa people have lived for centuries, with steam vents between the houses, the carved St Faith's church and Tamatekapua meeting house. The lakefront path runs from it into town. It is the most atmospheric part of Rotorua and the least like a tourist attraction.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the lake and the living village rather than the resort strip
pros: Lakefront path and the village on the doorstep
Genuine Te Arawa marae rather than a display
Five minutes on foot to the town centre
cons: Respect for a residential marae is expected rather than optional

name: City Centre and Eat Streat
tagline: Tutanekai Street, the Government Gardens and the museum
description: The compact centre running from the lakefront up Tutanekai Street, with the covered Eat Streat restaurant strip, the shops and the bus connections. The Government Gardens with the mock-Tudor Bath House sit at the eastern end and the Polynesian Spa is beside them. Everything practical in Rotorua is within a ten-minute walk.
bestFor: Short stays wanting restaurants, services and the gardens on foot
pros: Restaurants, shops and buses all within ten minutes
Government Gardens and the thermal spa nearby
Best connectivity and rental supply in town
cons: The highest rents in the town
Empty and quiet outside the season

name: Whakarewarewa and the Redwoods
tagline: At the forest edge, where the mountain bike trails start
description: The southern side of town where the Whakarewarewa forest begins, holding the Redwoods and a mountain bike network of well over a hundred trails that is the reason many people come to Rotorua at all. The thermal village and Te Puia are on the same side. Housing is ordinary suburban at moderate rents.
bestFor: Mountain bikers and runners who want the trailhead at the end of the street
pros: The Redwoods trail network directly accessible
Te Puia and the thermal valley nearby
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes into the centre

name: Ngongotaha
tagline: The lakeside village on the western shore
description: A separate village eight kilometres northwest along the lake, with its own shops, a trout stream, the gondola up Mount Ngongotaha and a much quieter residential character. Rents are lower than in town and the lake views from the western shore are the better ones, looking back across the water towards the city.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a quiet lakeside village with the town ten minutes away
pros: Quieter and cheaper than central Rotorua
Lake views back towards the city
Own shops and the gondola nearby
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes by car into town

name: Lynmore and Owhata
tagline: The eastern suburbs, family-quiet and best value
description: The residential districts east of the centre towards Lake Rotorua's eastern shore, with family houses, good local schools and a settled population that has nothing to do with tourism. Rents are the lowest in Rotorua for a decent house, the sulphur smell is weaker on this side, and the town centre is ten minutes by car.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting space and lower rents, with a car
pros: The lowest rents for a house in Rotorua
Noticeably less sulphur than the western side
cons: Ten minutes by car to anything
Nothing to do locally in the evening
